note: One entry per DEPLOY, newest first, timestamped in ET. Written for the trader, not for developers: each line says what he would NOTICE. The time matters - four deploys landed on 2026-08-31, so 'that day' cannot answer 'was that fix in the build I was running at 3pm?'. Add a new entry at the TOP each time something ships.

releases.heading: Long Term: an "i" next to every term explains it in plain words
items: Tap the small i next to MOS, the tiles, every checklist line (ROIC, EPS growth, debt payable…), every valuation line (sticker, P/E, Buffett value, Safety Buy…) and every line of the LEAP box (delta, breakeven, open interest, time value, the deep call) to read what it means and what the page wants it to be. Tap again to close it.
It works the same on the phone: the explanation opens right under the term and never filters the table or closes the drawer.

releases.heading: Long Term: the page no longer gets stuck on 'Loading Long Term…' on the phone
items: On the iPhone app the page could sit on 'Loading Long Term…' for hours with every tile at 0, even though the server had the rows. Its first request for rows never answered (an app resumed from the background can leave one hanging) and the page kept waiting on it instead of asking again.

Now a request that has not answered in 45 seconds is dropped and asked again, and coming back to the app re-asks straight away. If the rows still cannot load, the page says so with a Retry button instead of spinning.

releases.heading: Long Term: the page always opens with every row
items: The BUY / LEAPS / WAIT / AVOID / NO DATA tile you tap last is no longer remembered. Before, a tile left on (NO DATA on the phone) hid every row the next time you opened the page; now each visit starts with all rows and you tap a tile only to narrow them. The 50% / 30% margin choice and the sort are still remembered.
While the nightly filings refresh is running the page can take 10 seconds or more to show its rows; it says 'Loading Long Term…' until then.

releases.heading: Long Term: numbers re-checked against the SEC filings; Deckers now shows as a LEAPS candidate, debt reads in full
items: Every number on ten tickers (ADBE, QCOM, PYPL and seven others) was re-derived by hand from the SEC filings, Finnhub and the Schwab chain. ADBE BUY + LEAPS, QCOM LEAPS and PYPL AVOID all reproduce exactly: sticker, Safety Buy, LEAPS level and the contracts.

Deckers (DECK) was hidden: its 6-for-1 split was not recognised, so its old earnings read six times too high and its growth 5% instead of 36%. It now reads WAIT with the LEAPS flag (sticker about $153, LEAPS at or under about $122; BUY at the 30% margin).

Debt now includes the part due within a year for companies that file it separately (Adobe $6.4B, was $4.8B; Qualcomm, L3Harris, Conoco, Exxon, Celestica, PayPal). ROIC and the debt test are a little lower and more honest; ADBE and QCOM keep their verdicts, Celestica moves to AVOID.

Hershey's earnings now come from its own filings (about $8.84 a share) instead of a broken Finnhub figure; still AVOID. Qualcomm's dividends now count in its equity growth. The Why drawer says 'dividends missing' instead of 'buybacks/dividends missing' when only dividends are absent.
Weekend note: Schwab shows open interest 0 on most option strikes on Saturday and Sunday, so the LEAP contract under a badge may change on Monday's open.

releases.heading: Long Term: 'No data' drops from 220 tickers to a few dozen; every other row now says AVOID or WAIT with its reason
items: Most of the 220 'No data' rows were real companies whose SEC filings use a different tag for one number (Hershey's EPS, L3Harris's revenue, Verizon's capex, Oracle's debt). The page now reads those tags, fills a missing year from a second tag only when the two agree, and derives EPS from net income and share count when a year has no EPS tag.

Companies with 3 to 7 clean years are scored and capped at WAIT ('young: 4 years, BUY needs 8'). Companies with no revenue yet (QuantumScape, Oklo, NuScale...) read AVOID 'no revenue yet'. A company that loses money reads AVOID 'losing money' even when its history is short.

When the SEC and Finnhub disagree, the row is judged on the less favourable number: if that already fails a test the row reads AVOID with the reason ('ROIC 6% < 15% (sources differ on EPS)'); a missing cross-check scores the row but caps it at WAIT ('not cross-checked: ...'). Nothing in this change can make a row BUY or LEAPS that could not before. PayPal drops from BUY to AVOID: its debt was counted without the part due within a year (10.9B instead of 13.3B, PayPal's own total), and with the full debt its ROIC is 14%, just under the 15% bar. ADBE (BUY + LEAPS) and QCOM (LEAPS) remain.

Exxon and NextEra no longer show 'stale': their 2026 quarterly filings sit under a second SEC number that is now merged in. Exchange-traded notes such as VXX are listed with the ETFs instead of as a bank. A company with too little history but a ROIC already under 15% on either source reads AVOID with that number instead of 'No data' (NextEra, Conoco, Alibaba, On, STMicro).
The new numbers appear after the backend restarts and the nightly pass has run; until then the page shows yesterday's rows.

releases.heading: Long Term: the LEAP pick now follows the chain page's ENTRY rule, 3 to 12 months out
items: The contract under the LEAPS badge is now the out-of-the-money call just under 0.20 delta with the most open interest, the way the Options chain marks ENTRY, on the farthest expiry 3 to 12 months out (was the deep 0.75-delta call 12 to 25 months out).

The Why drawer's 'LEAP to buy' box shows that ENTRY-style contract in full and, under it, one line with the deep 0.75-delta call (the Rule #1 stock substitute, now the strike with the most open interest near 0.75) so you can compare the two.
After 16:00 ET Schwab hides option deltas; the row then says so and keeps retrying on its own instead of showing 'no contract'. A thin contract (open interest under 50) is still flagged ⚠ thin.

releases.heading: Scanner + BOT: Confirm L1 / L2 / L3 no longer flicker off between scans
items: RVOL only changes when a bar closes, but the scanner refreshes every minute or so. Before, a refresh that repeated the same RVOL number counted as 'not rising', so Confirm L1/L2/L3 showed for about a minute per 5-minute bar and was usually missing.
Now each timeframe compares with its last DIFFERENT RVOL number (your 'Last change' choice). Confirm stays on while RVOL is up and drops when a number falls.
The tag still needs 3+ Setup types and RVOL rising on 3+ timeframes, so it stays rare. After the app opens it needs one new bar before the first Confirm can show.
The BOT's Level 1/2/3 trades switch to the same rule after the scanner restarts tonight.

releases.heading: Long Term: the Why checklist reads in plain numbers
items: The checklist in the Why drawer now shows '✓ ROIC now 44% ≥ 15%', 'Sales growth 17%/yr', 'Debt payable 0.4× FCF', 'EPS $17.92', '10 years' and '1.07× last FY' instead of raw figures like 0.44065335753176044.

releases.heading: Long Term: the LEAP contract to buy, picked from the live option chain
items: Every row with the LEAPS badge now shows the contract under it: expiry, strike, ask and breakeven (for example 'Jan 2028 $200 C · ask $62.40 · BE $262 (+9%)'). It is the in-the-money call nearest 0.75 delta on the farthest expiry 12 to 25 months out, read from Schwab's chain when the page loads.

Click the row: the Why drawer has a new 'LEAP to buy' box with the full contract - days to expiry, delta, bid/ask/mid, cost per contract, breakeven and how far the price must move, time value, open interest, and a warning when the spread is wide.

Fail-safe: when the chain is down, the price is missing or no in-the-money call has a live two-sided quote, the row says 'No contract' and why. Nothing is suggested for rows without the LEAPS badge. The page picks the contract; the trade is yours.

releases.heading: Scanner + BOT: Mag7 BULL/BEAR counts, SPY/QQQ in every Setup rule, bear Confirm levels, AI scorecard for every rule
items: Mag7 only: the BULL/BEAR button now shows how many tickers pass each side, e.g. BULL ↑ 3 ↓7 = 3 pass bull, 7 pass bear. Flip to BEAR to see the bear list.
Mag7 now also scans SPY and QQQ (12 tickers). It no longer follows My Watchlist.
SPY and QQQ now get MX A+, Market turn, SOLO, MomoX A+, chart arrows and GO/OPT tags like a stock. The BOT already traded them; now the Setup column matches. Every other ETF stays out.
Bear scanner: Confirm L1 / L2 / L3 now show for puts too (same rules, mirrored), and the BOT trades bear Level 1/2/3 puts.
BOT: new Chart squeeze and Warning rules. The AI review now gives every Setup rule a fair share of its daily reviews instead of the busiest rules taking them all.

BOT page: new 'Every Setup rule · AI scorecard' box - each rule's trades, win %, average return, today's result, and the one chart check that helped it most. Each night the AI picks one check to paper-test for 10 trading days; it is kept only if it passes the statistics check. Nothing changes your real trades.

releases.heading: Long Term: more companies scored, debt checks tightened
items: Amazon, Lilly, CrowdStrike, Atlassian and others now get a score. Their filings use labels the first night's pass missed, so they showed short history or stale before.
Companies whose filings label their debt differently are no longer stuck on "debt unresolved". Their real debt is read and checked.
A company is called "no debt" only when its interest bill and Finnhub both agree. When Finnhub shows much more debt than the filings, the row says "Check data: debt understated?" instead of scoring.
A loss-making company now reads AVOID "losing money" instead of "Check data".
Exxon now maps to its real filings.

releases.heading: Fix: the saved copy of the app server could not start
items: Nothing changes on screen today: the running app already had the fix.

The saved copy of the server had the BOT and Truth check pages tangled together, so a fresh install or restore would have failed to start the app. It is straightened out and a test now checks the saved copy every time.

releases.heading: New: Long Term page (Buffett / Rule #1 screen)
items: A new Long Term page in the left panel scores every ticker from your watchlist and lists with the Buffett / Rule #1 method - no typing needed.
The numbers come from ten years of SEC filings plus Finnhub, refreshed every night.

BUY means a Rule #1 business trading at or under its Safety Buy price. WAIT is a good business whose price is above the buy level, or that is still too young or whose earnings are falling. AVOID is a business that fails the Rule #1 checks. The LEAPS flag means the price is under the level where long-dated calls are worth a look.
WAIT rows show the price to wait for: "BUY ≤ $X · LEAPS ≤ $Y".
Buys are rare by design: the default safety margin is 50%, and a 30% switch at the top loosens it.
A missing or stale price shows "No price" and is never marked BUY.
ETFs and names that have no SEC filings are listed at the bottom as not scored.
Tap or click a row for the why: the checklist, the ten-year table and the valuation in plain words.

releases.heading: Scanner: 21 / 50 EMA Touch lists use your Momox_2NEW! volume and close filters
items: On the 21 and 50 EMA Touch lists only, a scan match now needs 4h volume up at least 1.0% and the 1h close up at least 0.5% versus 2 bars ago - the same as your TOS Momox_2NEW! scan.
Watchlist, Mag7 and every other list keep 0.5% volume and 0.3% close, as before.
A ticker the stricter filter stops still shows on the EMA list when 'Scan matches only' is off, just not as a match.
Bear side: the same 1.0% volume, and a 1h close DROP of at least 0.5%.

releases.heading: Scanner: 21 / 50 EMA Touch lists now use your exact TOS rule
items: A ticker is on '21 EMA Touch' when the current bar's low is at or below the 21 EMA and its high is at or above it - the same as your TOS line 'low <= ema21 and high >= ema21'. Same for 50.
The EMA now includes the current bar's close, like TOS ExpAverage(close, 21). Before, it used the last finished bar's EMA.
The extra 'must be in an uptrend' check is gone, because your TOS script has none. Falling stocks that tag the EMA now show too, so the lists are longer.
Works on Monthly, Weekly and Daily - pick with the EMA chart dropdown as before.

releases.heading: Scanner: new Confirm L1 / L2 / L3 rules, and you can filter by them in Setup ▾
items: Every Confirm level now needs 3 or more Setup types, including Confirm L1 on the scanner (before, only the BOT checked this).
Confirm L1: RVOL cyan/green on 3 or more timeframes (5m to D), each one higher than the last scan, plus 3+ Setup types.
Confirm L2: L1 plus ONE of 2h / 4h / Daily SQZ that is cyan, blank, or fired today. Before, L2 needed both a cyan-or-all-blank SQZ AND a SQZ fire, and Weekly counted.
Confirm L3: L2 plus one or more cyan/green Skittles boxes from 2h to Monthly.
The Setup ▾ list now has Confirm L1+, Confirm L2+ and Confirm L3 tick-boxes. L1+ shows L1, L2 and L3 tickers; L2+ shows L2 and L3. The BOT's Level 1/2/3 trades use the same new rules.

releases.heading: Settings: renew Schwab from app.agxtrade.com on any computer, and see your full app keys
items: Renew both now works from app.agxtrade.com on any computer by pasting. Click Renew both and sign in to Schwab; the page it lands on will not load - copy its whole address into the Market Data callback URL box and click Complete Market Data OAuth.

Then click the new Open Accounts & Trading login button, sign in, paste that address into the Accounts & Trading box and click Complete Optional Trading OAuth. The line under the buttons says which step you are on and which box to use.

A paste in the wrong box, or from an older attempt, now says so in plain words (for example 'This address is from the Market Data sign-in') instead of 'mismatching_state'. Paste straight away: Schwab's address works for only about 30 seconds.
Your full Schwab app keys now show next to Market Data and Accounts & Trading, so you can check them against developer.schwab.com. The secrets stay hidden.

releases.heading: BOT page: Paper 5 rules must pass a statistics check before they switch on
items: The nightly AI planner tries a new Paper 5 rule each day. Before, a rule that did well in its 10-day paper test switched on by itself, even if it was just the lucky one out of many tries.
Now it must also pass a statistics check that counts every rule the planner has tried. The more rules tried, the higher the bar, so a lucky rule stays off.
As you asked, a rule that passes both still switches on automatically, with no click needed. The BOT page shows 'Statistics check: passed / not passed' and who switched it on.
An Approve / Reject box is ready if you ever want to sign off on rules yourself. It stays hidden unless that mode is turned on. Live money is not affected; this is Paper 5 paper trading only.

releases.heading: Paper 3 / Paper 5: orders go out within seconds and no longer miss the trade
items: Paper orders used to go out about 4 minutes after the BOT took a signal, at a price that was already old. They now go out within seconds, at the live bid/ask mid. Since Oct 19, orders sent within 3 minutes filled 46% of the time, later ones only 26%.

As you asked ('don't miss any trade'), a buy that has not filled at the mid after 2 minutes is no longer cancelled. It is sent again at the ask so it fills, up to 2 more times while the BOT still holds the trade. There is no spread filter.
Paying the ask costs more per trade. Across all BOT trades, buying at the ask and selling at the bid averaged about -25% a trade, so watch the Truth check to see whether the extra fills pay for it.
Selling is unchanged (limit at the mid). Your limits of 8 open, 25 a day and the 9:30-11:00 / 1:00-3:30 entry windows are unchanged and still skip many signals.
The Truth check card on the BOT page has a new line, 'Since the new order rules', so you can see the fill rate and results of the new orders on their own.

releases.heading: Scanner: switching an EMA list to Weekly or Daily no longer leaves a scanner error behind
items: After you switched the 21 EMA Touch list from Monthly to Weekly to Daily, the scanner kept trying to rebuild the old Monthly and Weekly lists every 15 seconds and failing each time. The scanner's status showed 'Unknown list 21 EMA Touch Monthly' even though every list on screen was fine.
The old list now stops as soon as you switch, so the scanner spends no time on lists you are not using.
The 21 and 50 EMA Touch lists keep their place in the rebuild order (right after Mag7 and Watchlist) on whichever timeframe you pick. Before, a 21 list on Daily dropped to the back of the queue.
The list picker (Mag7 ▾) now shows as soon as the scanner opens. Before, it could be missing for the first 15 seconds.

releases.heading: BOT page: new Truth check shows what your paper account really got next to what the BOT claims
items: A new Truth check card at the top of the BOT page puts the BOT's numbers next to your real Alpaca paper orders on the same signals, for the last 30 days.
It shows how many of your mid-price orders actually filled. Since Oct 19, Paper 3 filled 105 of 317 and Paper 5 filled 22 of 75. Most never filled.
On the trades that did fill, it shows what the BOT says against what the paper account got: Paper 3 BOT -6.3% vs paper -10.7%, Paper 5 BOT +27.9% vs paper +11.6%.
It lists the BOT's biggest wins your paper account never got, for example AAPL 11-04 +232%, where the $3.15 limit order did not fill. Open 'By rule' to see the same split for each rule.
An option with a $0 bid at the exit now counts as $0 on the BOT page and in the scanner's Record column, because nobody would buy it. Before, a few penny options showed as +100% winners.

releases.heading: Scanner: 21 / 50 EMA Touch lists fixed for former SPACs (OUST, BBAI, DJT, GRAB)
items: On the Monthly chart, OUST, BBAI, DJT and GRAB had EMA lines built partly from years of flat prices from before they started trading (the old SPAC shell). OUST's monthly 50 EMA showed about $37.53 when the real line is about $29.

Those flat months are now skipped, so these four tickers join or leave the 21 / 50 EMA Touch lists on their real lines. A ticker with fewer than 100 real months still sits out the Monthly 50 list, the same as any newer stock.
Every other ticker was checked against a full-history EMA (AAPL, NVDA, MSFT, CVS and others) and already matched to within a few cents on Daily, Weekly and Monthly.

releases.heading: Sectors: Technology card sized correctly again
items: SK Hynix (SKHY) filled almost the whole Technology card while NVIDIA, Apple and Microsoft shrank to slivers. Its market cap had been read in Korean won as if it were dollars (TSMC and Tencent were also too big, in their home currencies).
Tiles now only use a live market cap when it is in US dollars and close to the company's real size; otherwise they use the built-in size. The biggest names are the biggest tiles again.

releases.heading: Settings: Renew both Schwab logins with one click - nothing to paste
items: New Renew both button (Settings, Schwab). Log in to Schwab once in the window that opens and click Allow; the window then goes on to the Accounts & Trading approval by itself. The line under the buttons shows Step 1 of 2, Step 2 of 2, then the new expiry.
No more copying the https://127.0.0.1/?code=... address: the PC now finishes both logins itself. Before, the Accounts & Trading login could never finish on its own.
Renew from the PC - Schwab sends the login back to the PC itself. On the phone the callback boxes still work as before.

First time only: Chrome may show Your connection is not private after the Schwab login - click Advanced, then Continue to 127.0.0.1. Running scripts	rust_schwab_callback_cert.ps1 once removes that page for good.

releases.heading: The app comes back much faster after a restart
items: On every restart the backend used to read the whole saved option-chain history (most of the 2.7 GB database) before answering, so the app showed 'API unavailable' for 10-15 minutes or more. It now samples that table instead and starts in seconds.
If any startup step is ever slow again, the backend log names it ('[startup] database: ... took Ns'), so the cause is visible right away.

releases.heading: Scanner: complete early-morning bars for every Watchlist ticker
items: Watchlist tickers that are not also in Mag7 could miss part of the 4-7 AM premarket (and part of the overnight) for the whole day, which made their early 1h/2h/4h RVOL and gates read low. Every ticker now gets the full window.
For about one scan in twelve, some rows briefly lost last night and the premarket after a background re-read, so values could flicker for one scan. That no longer happens.

releases.heading: Sector pages now look like Robinhood's: names, chips and a clean list
items: A sector's page now reads like Robinhood's: big title, today's % (from the sector ETF), a line about the sector, then 'In this list' with every stock.
Each row shows the company name with the ticker underneath, and the price on the right in green or orange with today's % below it.
Chips under the description narrow the list to a sub-group, for example Technology: Semiconductors, Software, Internet, Hardware.
Sort by Size, High or Low, and switch between List and Map (the heatmap) at the top of the list; both choices are remembered.
Company names appear once the backend has restarted with this update; until then rows show the ticker only.

releases.heading: Sectors: tap a sector to open it, like Robinhood
items: Tap a sector's name (for example Technology >) to open that sector's own page: its move today, a bigger heatmap with about 40 of its stocks, and a list of every one of them.
The list shows each stock's price, today's % and market cap, and sorts by Size, High (best move first) or Low (worst first). Your choice is remembered.
Tap any tile or row to open that ticker's chart. 'All sectors' at the top takes you back.
The extra stocks are only fetched while a sector's page is open, so the Sectors grid is no heavier than before.

releases.heading: Scanner keeps updating after 8 PM ET
items: After 8 PM the scanner stopped at its 7:55 PM bar until midnight, and showed an amber note like 'window ended 184m ago'. It now picks up the overnight bars from 8 PM on (about 16 minutes behind, like before midnight).
The note next to UPDATED is in plain words: 'market closed' on weekends, and 'no new bar for 1h 30m' only when the data really is behind.

releases.heading: MomX board: new Price and Spread columns
items: New Price column right after % Chg: the stock's current price (the live quote when there is one). Click the header to sort.

New Spread column: how wide this ticker's options trade. Tight (under 3%) and OK (3-8%) usually fill at the mid; Wide (8-15%) means price above the mid or skip; Avoid (over 15%, or an at-the-money option under $3 that is 30 cents or more wide) means skip. In paper trading, mid orders filled 72% of the time on Tight names, 50% on OK, and 16% on Wide and Avoid.

It looks at the nearest Friday weekly and the next monthly expiry: 5 strikes around the stock price, calls and puts. Hover (or tap on the phone) to see the median spread in % and $, which expiries were used, and when the chain was read.

It is filled in 10:00-15:30 ET from option chains the app already loads (no extra Schwab calls), so it shows '-' before 10:00 and for tickers whose chain has not been read in the last hour. After 15:30 the day's last reading stays up until midnight. History shows '-' because spreads are not archived.

releases.heading: Sectors: scrolls to every sector, sorts by High/Low, and sits on the phone's bottom bar
items: The Sectors page now scrolls on the phone and on desktop. Before, only the first few sectors could be reached.
New Default / High / Low switch at the top of Sectors: High puts the best-moving sector first, Low the worst. Your choice is remembered.
Phone bottom bar is now Chart, Options, Sectors, Premarket, MomX, More. Alerts moved into More, and the More button shows the unseen-alert count so a new alert is still visible.
The % on each sector card is that sector's ETF move (Technology = XLK), so it can differ by a hundredth or two from Robinhood's own figure.

releases.heading: New Sectors panel: Robinhood-style sector heatmap with each sector's top stocks
items: New Sectors page: on the phone tap More, then Sectors; on desktop it is in the left menu, or open it as a panel from the option chain's + menu in Charts & OI. You get 11 sector cards (Technology, Financials, Healthcare, Consumer Cyclical, Communication, Industrials, Consumer Defensive, Energy, Utilities, Real Estate, Materials), each with that sector's 16 biggest stocks, like the Robinhood Sectors card.
The % at the top right of each card is the whole sector's move today, from its sector ETF (Technology = XLK, Financials = XLF, Energy = XLE...).

RH look matches the Robinhood card: the biggest names in a tall top row, then shorter rows, and the bottom row shows tickers only. Green is full at +2.5% and orange at -2%. The Technology card holds the same names as Robinhood's, including GOOGL, AMZN and META.

A switch at the top picks RH (white cards) or TOS (dark thinkorswim-style treemap, green and red); your choice is remembered. Tap any tile to open that ticker's chart (on the Sectors page it opens at 5m, like Premarket and Auto Alert). The ticker on the chart is outlined.

Prices update every 8 seconds. Tile sizes start from built-in market caps and switch to live ones over the first few minutes. A stock the quote feed has no price for is left out instead of shown as a blank tile.

releases.heading: New: option spread scanner (python scripts\option_spread_scan.py)
items: Lists the option the Bot would buy for every scanner ticker (calls and puts) with bid, ask, spread %, the dollar cost of one contract's round trip, open interest, volume and how old the chain is - tightest first, marked TIGHT (10% or less), OK (10-15%) or WIDE (over 15%).

Why it matters, tested on your recorded Bot trades: the typical trade gave up about a quarter of its price to the bid/ask spread in and out. On days the rule never saw (Oct 27 - Nov 2), skipping wide-spread options raised the average trade by 14-24 points whenever the fill was worse than the mid, better on 5 of 5 days. Tighter is always cheaper; 10%/15% are practical lines, not a proven best cut-off.

Run it from the app folder: .venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts\option_spread_scan.py  (options: --list Mag7, --side call or put, --top 20, --csv file.csv). It reads the app's saved chains only - no extra Schwab calls.

releases.heading: Ticker popup: OI levels appear within a second or two
items: The ⚡ popup now draws the OI levels from any option chain captured earlier today, right away. Open interest only changes overnight, so those walls are today's. The age of the chain is printed under Strike reach (e.g. "chain data from 12:47 ET, 68 min old").
Checked on AMZN and MSFT: levels on the chart and the walls list within a few seconds, on desktop and at phone width. A chain from yesterday is still never shown as today's.

releases.heading: Option chains keep refreshing all day (levels and charts no longer go stale)
items: Big tickers' option chains (AMZN, NVDA) could stop refreshing for 30 to 70 minutes in the middle of the day. One slow read of six months of option history made every other chain refresh wait in line. That read no longer holds anyone up.
You'll notice: the ⚡ popup's OI levels, the OI page and the chart walls stay current instead of showing a chain from an hour ago, and popups stop sitting on "reading the option chain…".
Takes effect after the next backend restart.

releases.heading: Ticker popup: OI levels show on every ticker, and the mini chart opens faster
items: The ⚡ ticker popup now draws the High-OI levels (strike + OI lines and the ±EM2 edges) on the chart for big option chains like AMZN too. Before, the popup refused any chain more than 15 seconds old, so a large chain could sit on "reading the option chain…" for a minute with no levels at all. Now a chain captured in the last 15 minutes is used straight away; yesterday's chain is still never shown as today's.
The popup's mini chart opens instantly when you reopen a ticker you already looked at, then refreshes behind the scenes. Same on desktop and phone.

releases.heading: Live RVOL: the forming candle updates every 5 seconds, like TOS
items: The RVOL cells (5m to 4h) for the rows on your screen now rescore the candle that is forming right now from the live Schwab stream every 5 seconds, with your exact TOS formula and colours. Before, they waited for the next scanner build (about 3 minutes old by the time you saw them).

Only shown when the stream has every minute of that candle; otherwise the scanner's regular value stays. Replayed on this morning's candles: 4,715 of 4,715 live values matched the correct number and colour.
Display only: alerts, Confirm badges, filters, sorting and the bot still use the scanner's regular values.

releases.heading: RVOL 1h / 2h / 4h now score the current bar, like TOS
items: At 11:06 the scanner's 1h and 2h RVOL were still scoring the finished 10:00-11:00 hour (NVTS 1h 3.0, 2h 3.2) while TOS had moved to the new 11:00 bar (blank). Those columns are built from 30-minute candles that lagged; their newest part now comes from the live 5-minute candles, so 1h/2h/4h always include the bar that is forming now. 4h and D already matched TOS.

releases.heading: Mag7 no longer stuck on old candles after a stream gap
items: After the 10:16 restart Mag7 sat on the 10:10 candle for about 30 minutes: a gap in the live stream blocked the live candles, yet the scanner still treated Mag7 as 'kept fresh by the stream' and postponed its normal candle refresh. A ticker blocked by a gap now gets its normal refresh right away (takes effect at the next scanner restart, after the close).

releases.heading: Scanner RVOL catches up with TOS: live candles no longer late
items: The live Schwab candles that keep the scanner's 5m/15m RVOL current were arriving 6+ minutes late, because the app re-saved every 1-minute candle since August (2.6 million) every 30 seconds. It now keeps the last 4 days only (all the scanner and charts use), so the forming candle reaches the scanner within about a minute, like TOS.

releases.heading: No more blank screen when the app updates
items: On weekdays 4 AM-8 PM ET a new version no longer reloads the screen in front of you (that is what blanked the scanner this morning). It updates itself the moment you switch away or lock the phone, so you come back to the new version. A thin "New version available" bar shows meanwhile if you want it now. Outside those hours updates apply as before.
The scanner's UPDATED line no longer shows "oldest start ...m ago" (how far back its candle history reaches); hover the line for full details.

releases.heading: H/L⚡ is the default order when no column is sorted
items: Tap a column header and the board sorts by that column. Tap it until the arrow goes away (or tick H/L⚡ sort) and the board goes back to H/L⚡ order. Bear board and NEWS keep the scanner's own order.

releases.heading: Clicking a column header always sorts by that column
items: With "H/L⚡ sort" switched on, clicking Time (or any column) showed the arrow but the rows stayed in H/L order, so Time read 08:25, 08:40, 09:08, 08:20. Clicking a header now switches H/L⚡ sort off, so the board really sorts by the column you clicked. Tick H/L⚡ sort again any time to go back.

releases.heading: AI agents stay off during the trading day
items: This morning the AI agents' model took most of the laptop's processor, so the app would not load and the scanner lagged. The agents now run only on weekday evenings, nights and weekends; from 6:30 AM to 5 PM ET they stay off so the scanner and charts get the whole processor. Nothing about trading or the scanner's rules changed.

releases.heading: Record column reads "AI - 62%"
items: The Record column's win % is now written "AI - 62%" (was "AI 62%"), as asked.

releases.heading: Record column says "AI" instead of "Overall"
items: The Record column's win % now reads "AI 62%" instead of "Overall 62%". Same number: how often the 100 most similar past trades won. Tap or hover it for the full explanation.

releases.heading: No more backup window popping up; unsupervised research reads the full trade picture
items: The Google Drive backup (12:30 AM and 2:45 PM CT) no longer opens a black window on the screen. It runs silently and writes what it did to artifacts/agx-backup.log.

The unsupervised research on the BOT page (market-mood groups and the 'unusual trade' detector) had been looking at only 4 of its inputs - market direction, setups and levels were missing - so last night's result meant nothing. It now uses every saved input and was re-run on the full history. Still research only: it never filters or sizes a trade.

releases.heading: AI agents finish their reviews without taking over the laptop
items: Every agent review tonight failed: each AI call was cut off after 3 minutes, while loading the model and reading 8 trades takes longer on this laptop. Calls now get 10 minutes; they are research only and never touch trades.
The local AI model now uses at most 4 CPU cores. Before, it took the whole processor whenever an agent asked it something, which would slow the scanner and charts during the trading day.

releases.heading: Record column: one overall win %
items: The Record column now leads with one overall win %: of the 100 past trades whose picture looked most like this row (RVOL, Skittles, squeeze, ADX, high/low, grade, sector), how many won. The all-trades rate sits beside it. Tap for the per-rule figures.
It is marked "unproven": tested on the 3 newest days it had not seen, it was no better than a coin flip for calls and only slightly better for puts. Treat it as context, not a signal.
Level 1-3, Setup tags and chart levels only started being saved with trades today, so they join the overall % automatically as those trades build up.

releases.heading: AI agents run 24/7; five new agents; Record shows every win %
items: The AI research agents now run around the clock. During the trading day (4 AM-8 PM ET) they take one batch of trades every 5 minutes so the scanner stays fast; overnight and on weekends they run back-to-back.

Five new agents study your recorded trades: the option contract (price, spread, delta, days to expiry), time of day, sector, distance to the nearest OI wall, and market turns. Like the others, each is scored on whether its calls come true.

The scanner Record column now shows the win % of every rule on the row (for example "GO 58% · RVOL 51%") instead of "2 rule histories". Each figure is that rule's real last-10-day result, never a combined guess.

releases.heading: Hermes, OpenClaw and the nightly AI retrain fixed
items: Hermes research works again. Its settings pointed at a folder that only exists inside the Codex app, so every review failed instantly. It also gets 7 minutes instead of 3: on this laptop Hermes needs about 2 minutes just to start.
OpenClaw can start again outside the Codex app (its Node runtime lives in the Codex app folder).
The local AI model now stays loaded for 30 minutes instead of 5, so most reviews skip a 50-second reload.

The nightly AI retrain had not finished since Friday 10-30: every scanner restart started another copy and four fought each other at the lowest priority. Only one runs at a time now, at a priority that lets it finish.

releases.heading: Watchlist aims for under a minute per refresh
items: The scanner now gets the same share of the CPU as the chart server instead of leftovers. Windows was also throttling its calculation helpers to about a fifth of a core each; that is switched off.
News headlines no longer hold up a Watchlist refresh: the board shows the latest headlines it has and fetches newer ones in the background. Only the first refresh after a restart waits for news.
Charts and the scanner now share the CPU evenly, so with thinkorswim busy a chart may open a little slower than before.

releases.heading: Today's scanner fixes combined with the GitHub version
items: The faster-refresh fixes and your list order (Mag7, Watchlist, 21 EMA, 50 EMA) now sit on top of the GitHub version: Friday's scanner behaviour, the Record column changes and the BOT research updates.

releases.heading: Scanner refreshes faster; your list order
items: Scanner priority is now your order: 1. Mag7, 2. Watchlist, 3. 21 EMA, 4. 50 EMA, then the other lists.
The Watchlist no longer waits behind another list's news download. A list now hands over its turn as soon as its own scan is done, so the next one starts right away.
Per-ticker news headlines are fetched 8 at a time instead of one by one, so each refresh spends far less time on news.

releases.heading: Scanner rows no longer vanish and come back
items: When the scanner was busy rebuilding, the page sometimes got a 'still building' answer with no rows and blanked the Watchlist for a refresh or two. It now keeps showing the last rows it had until fresh ones arrive.

Earlier this afternoon the scanner sat on 'Building this watchlist' for over an hour: a half-finished code update had been left in the live app and crashed its helper processes. That update was rolled back and the scanner restarted.

releases.heading: Self-learning research: market regimes, unusual entries, scored specialists
items: Each night the BOT groups trading days into market regimes on its own (no win/loss labels) and checks on later days whether the good regimes stayed good. See BOT > Unsupervised research.
A small neural network learns what normal entries look like and flags unusual ones; the BOT page shows whether unusual entries won more or less on later days and which inputs made them unusual.
Six new specialist agents: regime, anomaly, entry, exit, risk and news. Each makes a higher/lower call on the next batch, gets graded, and sees its own record next time (BOT > Specialist scoreboard).
All of this is paper research only: it never blocks, sizes or exits a trade, and promotion rules are unchanged.

releases.heading: OpenClaw and Hermes reviews work again; Record shows real results
items: OpenClaw reviews wrapped in a JSON code block are accepted again (restored after this morning's revert), so BOT reviews stop falling back to plain Ollama or 'unavailable'.
The BOT reviewer now talks to the BOT OpenClaw gateway that the start script launches, instead of your personal OpenClaw profile.
Hermes research replies are accepted when Hermes prints start-up lines or wraps its answer in a code block; prose answers are still rejected.

Record column shows each rule's checked win rate and trade count again, by rule name only (e.g. 'RVOL↑: 58% · n=41') instead of 'Learning' on every row. A validated P(win) still takes priority when one exists.

releases.heading: Scanner back to Friday's behaviour
items: Undid the Sunday and Monday scanner changes: Live no longer hides rows by study-candle date, and old unchanged scans are no longer reused, so Watchlist tickers show their full columns again.
EMA 21/50 lists go back to their earlier rules; the rebuilding and old-data messages return to their earlier wording.

releases.heading: Scanner RVOL is live again after the open
items: The Watchlist was stuck on 09:25 premarket candles all morning, so every RVOL number was a premarket reading. It now refreshes during the session (10:25 candles at 10:36).
Cause: closing out Friday's ~8,900 expired virtual BOT options rewrote a large file once per trade and held up every scanner board. Those close-outs are now saved in one batch.
The scanner's calculation processes now get a fair share of the CPU instead of only leftovers. With thinkorswim open, Mag7 had taken 16 minutes; it now takes about 15 seconds.

Charts load again while thinkorswim is busy. The chart server ran at a lower priority than thinkorswim and Chrome and could take 30+ seconds to answer; it now runs at normal priority, above the scanner.
History FIND search works again (it returned an error instead of results). Takes effect at the next scanner restart.

releases.heading: Scanner requests stay responsive during data refresh
items: Market-data loading status no longer blocks the board behind candle conversion. While status is busy, the board uses the last known loading count or marks it unknown.
The scanner HTTP service now gets CPU time above idle; calculation subprocesses explicitly remain idle. A larger request backlog handles the burst of requests when opening the scanner.

releases.heading: Setup no longer repeats the Time column
items: Setup omits the source timestamp when the same time already appears in the visible Time column. If Time is hidden or shows a different time, Setup keeps the source timestamp without the Data prefix.
MOM, SQZ fire, SKIT and chart-signal tags keep their own signal times. Study-age warnings remain in the cell tooltip.

releases.heading: Scanner requests avoid repeated EMA-list calculations
items: At startup, concurrent tape requests wait for the initial live-stream result without launching a large archive decode. If the live request fails, the existing saved-history fallback remains available.

Opening and polling the scanner no longer recalculate every EMA-touch universe just to read a list name or active selection. EMA universe reads still use current conditions, and list edits and timeframe switches are reflected immediately.

While a rebuild runs, repeated requests reuse the saved board without decoding the same large file again. New board replacements are picked up immediately; original market-data timestamps are preserved.
Heavy background agent discussions and native gateway autostart wait until after 8 PM ET on weekdays. Scanner signal capture, virtual trading and saved-model scoring remain available.

releases.heading: Entry-pattern research and agent reliability
items: Research agents now receive unsupervised groups of similar frozen Level, Setup and chart inputs. The BOT shows sample coverage; these groups are research clues, not win probabilities or automatic trade approvals.
Hermes research has a bounded timeout and records whether its last local-model request succeeded. Specialist findings are saved for review and testing before any virtual or paper model promotion.

releases.heading: Scanner remembers column sorting
items: Your selected sort column and direction return when you leave the scanner and come back or reload. Live, News and History retain their own ordering; bull and bear live sorts are separate.
Untouched live scanners keep the existing H/L default. Hidden or removed sort columns safely use an available default.

releases.heading: Cleaner scanner Time column
items: The Time column shows only the time for today’s study candles, without the Data prefix. Previous-date candles show month/day and time. Source-age warnings remain available separately.

releases.heading: Scanner responsiveness and clock updates
items: Scanner startup no longer waits for learning-memory recovery before opening its API.
Repeated scanner reads now skip worker startup and list-file reconciliation when the background supervisor is already running.
Live quote updates reuse scan filters instead of rebuilding them every second, and saved board data is read when switching lists rather than on every refresh.
Premarket polling runs only while the Premarket workspace is visible, so MomX and chart browsing no longer trigger its heavy background analysis.
Chart grade-history lookups search tape bytes without decoding the whole file. Scanner responses use compact JSON.
The header ET clock updates independently of dashboard data requests. Candle timestamps and age warnings still reflect the supplied market data.

releases.heading: Expanded research team and entry snapshot checks
items: Chart/indicator, market-regime, exit/risk and data-quality specialists join the learning team. Each completed batch runs up to three relevant specialist investigations; findings reach the reviewer, critic and experiment planner.
Normal and Star #1 signals preserve independent Level/Setup snapshots alongside completed chart context. Missing historical inputs remain unknown; the BOT learning panel reports snapshot coverage.

Hermes reviews use bounded output and process-tree timeout recovery. The dedicated OpenClaw startup distinguishes a starting process from a running listener and can recover a stalled startup. Research findings require later paper validation before supported changes can be promoted.

releases.heading: Live scanner hides old study rows
items: Live hides previous-trading-date rows such as 10/30, with Scan matches only checked or unchecked. Today’s available candles stay visible even when several minutes old.
Overnight starts at 8 PM ET and belongs to the following trading date. Undated rows stay hidden; recorded snapshots remain in History.

releases.heading: Phone scanner controls stay visible
items: Time and Pop-up cards wrap onto another line when needed instead of being cropped off the phone screen.
Long source-data timing notes wrap within the toolbar while the scanner table keeps horizontal scrolling.

releases.heading: Scan matches only checkbox restored
items: Scan matches only is checked by default. Uncheck it to see the whole selected list; check it again to hide nonmatches.
News and Filters apply to the rows selected by this checkbox.

releases.heading: Scanner shows matching tickers only
items: Nonmatching tickers stay hidden. News and Setup selections narrow the scan matches instead of bringing nonmatching tickers back.
Removed the switch that displayed the whole list. Saved matches retain their source candle timestamps while rebuilding.

releases.heading: EMA lists require TOS ALL plus ANY signals
items: EMA lists require Last >= $3, 4-hour EXT volume up at least 1%, 1-hour EXT close up at least 0.5% versus two bars ago, and candle low <= current EMA <= candle high on the selected chart timeframe.

Both 21 and 50 EMA lists reuse the Watchlist ANY group unchanged: momentum crosses (MACD, EMA 9/20 or EMA 4/8), squeeze-fire and RVOL. At least one signal must pass, in addition to all EMA-list conditions.

A visible EMA list gets priority for its first startup build. Completed results clear recovered worker connection errors. Source candle times remain visible; data-provider differences can affect TOS comparisons.

releases.heading: Scanner distinguishes rebuilding from old market candles
items: A completed scanner result clears the rebuilding message even if list metadata arrives late.
Saved results remain labeled while a list rebuilds. The message explains that Scan matches only filters rows; each Data timestamp remains the actual candle time, not the refresh time.

releases.heading: EMA timeframe switching stops obsolete scanner builds
items: Switching a 21 or 50 EMA list between Daily, Weekly and Monthly retires the previous timeframe worker, including switches made from another device.
Obsolete timeframe requests no longer keep retrying or leave an unknown-list error in scanner status. A build waiting its turn is cancelled when its timeframe is retired.

releases.heading: Less repeated scanner work on unchanged old data
items: Production build watching ignores generated output, runtime artifacts and logs so background rebuilds do not repeatedly compete with scanner and AI work.

The scanner can reuse unchanged study results when all source tapes are more than one day old. New or corrected candles, a new ET date and changed calculation settings force recalculation; original data timestamps remain visible.

The dedicated OpenClaw launcher retains a Node compile cache and uses the supported runtime for child helpers. Local Ollama remains the active review provider while native gateway reliability is verified.

Valid OpenClaw review JSON wrapped in a single JSON code block is accepted without an unnecessary fallback. Missing fields, invalid decisions and surrounding prose are still rejected; trading entry and exit rules are unchanged.

releases.heading: Record learns from frozen chart levels
items: New virtual and paper trade records retain completed 5-minute VWAP, EMA 9/21/50/200, observed premarket highs/lows and complete previous-session highs/lows with classical support/resistance pivots. Missing, stale and future chart values remain unknown.

Record neural training and agent reviews receive the frozen chart context alongside Levels 1–3 and Setup rules. Record details explain the inputs; older models cannot supply a chart-enabled probability without fresh validation. Outcomes exclude fees.

releases.heading: BOT and scanner calculations exclude fees
items: Record probability training now counts a win when the recorded Strategy-exit midpoint exceeds entry. Estimated fees are excluded. Previous fee-based models cannot supply the new probability; the new target must pass its own validation.
BOT experiment evaluation, recurring-loss memory and scanner rule history also exclude the assumed round-trip fee. Actual recorded prices and fills are preserved.

releases.heading: Structured BOT agent reviews
items: OpenClaw reviews now request structured JSON through the native gateway, preventing a prose response from being mistaken for a failed review. Local Ollama fallback remains available.

releases.heading: Record shows learning progress and validates future forecasts
items: Record shows Learning while evidence is insufficient, rather than an unexplained empty probability. Tap it for the training, calibration, held-out and future-evaluation requirements. A percentage can appear only for a matching entry forecast from a model that passed the fixed prospective trial.

Neural research freezes a candidate before future outcomes, verifies forecast timing and quote coverage, and checks calibration, win rate, total losses, net P/L and drawdown across 100 future trades and 10 entry days. Later independent monitoring can withdraw it. Existing positions and entry rules are unchanged.
RVOL learning now isolates the complete ET date, so the same day number in a later month cannot reuse old increasing-volume history.
BOT OpenClaw can use a dedicated local profile and restart separately from the scanner, preserving existing session history. Direct Ollama fallback remains available.

releases.heading: Record learns frozen Levels and all 23 Setup rules
items: New bullish BOT signals preserve their scanner Level, exact 23-rule Setup combination, distinct count and RVOL-increase evidence for nightly learning and agent review. A+ remains a grade input and MOM is optional. Old missing snapshots remain unknown.

Record now shows P(win) — while net-profit probability is unvalidated. Tap for current confirmation, Setup rules, training coverage and the separate experimental earlier-trade score. No invented probability is displayed.

A separate neural challenger uses quote-checked outcomes after estimated costs, separate training/calibration/test periods and duplicate-outcome checks. Model-quality specialists can investigate missing inputs; active trading rules are unchanged.
Scanner worker reloads target the worker entry file precisely, leaving validation jobs running.
Record detail headings remain readable above the text while you scroll on a phone.

releases.heading: Measure higher win rate and smaller losses before paper promotion
items: Paper experiments now report wins, losses, flat trades, net win rate and total losing-trade losses for the baseline and candidate. New candidates must improve both win rate and total losses as well as P/L and drawdown before promotion. These are evaluation requirements, not a claim of improved trading performance.
OpenClaw reviews have a bounded three-minute local-model response window before direct Ollama fallback. Agent reviews remain advisory and cannot delay trade entries or exits.

releases.heading: Choose A+ directly from the Setup column
items: The Setup selector now includes the same A+ grade shown in the table, separate from MX A+. Combine it with any existing rule using All or Any; your choice remains active after refresh.
The selector contains 24 choices: the A+ grade plus the original 23 Setup rules. BOT entry rules and Setup-type counts are unchanged.

releases.heading: Setup choices use the column’s symbols and colours
items: The Setup column selector now shows familiar symbols and tag styling, including 💥 Explosive, ⭐1, 🔥 Chart squeeze, filled MOM and cyan ADX (magenta on BEAR). Per-ticker values and times are not invented in the selector.

A checked Setup rule filters the table even when the old generic FILTERS switch was off. The toolbar and selector now report the same active state and matching count. Turning filtering off clears the column choices.

releases.heading: Setup selections match the visible table rules
items: Choose rules from Setup ▾ in the table header. Checking a rule immediately turns filtering on; the old single-Setup strategy, including AI score 55%+, no longer silently narrows the selection.
Explosive and Steady choices match the visible Setup pattern markers, excluding raw pattern values whose grade/pattern button is not displayed.
FILTERS ON/OFF is explicit. Your saved Setup choices remain active when reopening the board; Clear selections restores the unfiltered view.

releases.heading: Choose rules directly from the Setup column
items: Tap Setup ▾ in the scanner table header to choose any of the 23 rule types. The selector includes All/Any matching, select all, clear, and the existing Setup sort action.
Choosing rules immediately filters the table and replaces the old single-Setup strategy, so Explosive does not silently require AI score 55%+. Other filter settings are kept on standby.
The toolbar now shows FILTERS ON or OFF. Saved Setup selections apply when the scanner reopens; clearing selections returns to the unfiltered board.

releases.heading: Choose your own combination of Setup rules
items: Scanner filters now offer checkboxes for all 23 existing Setup rule types. Choose any combination, match all selected rules or any selected rule, select all, or clear the selection. No rules are preselected.

Selections use the same Setup signals as the column, save with your filters, and reset cleanly. MOM means the visible strong/filled tag. Selected checkbox requirements narrow the same ticker even when another Setup strategy is selected.

releases.heading: Paper 3 history stays visible while the broker reconciles
items: Paper 3 and Paper 5 can show their last saved account records while broker reconciliation is busy, with an explicit saved-snapshot notice. Broker calls no longer hold the history page loading.
Paper account order counts, P/L and tables appear before the AI discussion. Account rules are collapsible, and Refresh paper reloads the selected paper account.

Paper-history requests time out with a visible retry option. Switching accounts or ranges clears the prior view; an unavailable account is reported instead of staying on Loading or inventing zero trades.

releases.heading: Level reviews honor the selected AI provider
items: Level 1–3 completed-trade reviews now honor the same AI provider setting as other BOT trades. Selecting Ollama skips the unavailable OpenClaw attempt and its timeout delay.
Selecting OpenClaw retains local Ollama fallback. Reviews stay advisory; entries, exits, virtual trade history and broker-order rules are unchanged.
The AI status now distinguishes app-coordinated local Ollama reviews from native OpenClaw gateway reviews, so the displayed provider matches the selected route.

releases.heading: BOT trade counts separate missing prices from marked positions
items: The trade summary now separates closed trades with prices, open trades with usable marks, and unpriced trades. Missing exit quotes no longer appear as an additional open-position count beside the same unpriced trades.
Trade P/L, wins and losses still follow the selected contract and exit comparison. Best price remains an explicitly labelled hindsight view.

releases.heading: Local AI research configuration for BOT agents
items: The OpenClaw BOT research agents are configured to use local Ollama while ChatGPT is unavailable. Completed-trade reviews remain advisory; no entry, exit or broker-order rules changed.

Local Ollama responses passed a connectivity check. Native OpenClaw readiness and browser verification are separate checks; this configuration does not establish a reliable win probability or better trading performance.

releases.heading: BOT levels show their Setup rules
items: The Level strategies explanation now lists all 23 counted Setup types and explains that three distinct types are required, with MOM optional.
New level trades show their captured Setup rules directly below the strategy name, including on touch screens; multiple timeframes of one rule count once.

releases.heading: All trades adds Level 1–3 virtual strategies
items: All trades now has a Level strategy dropdown: All strategies, Level 1, Level 2 and Level 3. Selecting a level updates its trade list, P/L, leaderboard and history comparisons together.

New bullish level strategies require at least three distinct Setup types, with MOM optional. They reuse the scanner’s increasing-RVOL, SQZ-release and Skittles definitions; missing previous updates do not qualify. Each level records its own first signal per ticker/day, so the experiments overlap.

Entries use existing midpoint quote handling and strategy exits. New records retain their signal-time level and Setup types for the post-trade OpenClaw/ChatGPT/Ollama review flow. Earlier history is not relabelled or backfilled, and these virtual experiments do not place broker orders.

releases.heading: Scanner shows rising-RVOL confirmation levels
items: Setup now shows Confirm L1/L2/L3 when at least three cyan/green RVOL timeframes rise versus their previous valid scanner update. Equal/decreasing values remove qualification; first observations and missing history do not qualify.

L2 also requires cyan SQZ or all SQZ cells blank, plus an active Setup SQZ-release tag. L3 adds a cyan/green Skittles box from 2-hour through Monthly. These are rule confirmations, not probability percentages.

Repeated polls and renders do not advance RVOL history. Ticker/timeframe and list histories stay separate; stale live studies receive no confirmation badge. History replays loaded snapshots chronologically, using their own timestamps. Entries, exits and existing filters are unchanged.

releases.heading: Paper learning uses local Ollama directly
items: Paper review agents now use local Ollama as the primary model, avoiding ChatGPT gateway timeout waits. The learning-team banner shows the active provider.
Hermes remains independent research. Entries and exits do not wait for AI review; unvalidated research does not change active trading rules.

releases.heading: Scanner Record is compact again
items: Record shows a single AI - 50% style score when available, or a dash when missing or stale. Tap or hover for model context, history, wins, losses and data coverage. Scores below 55% can appear in Record; the AI filter keeps its existing 55% threshold.
Unavailable OpenClaw reviews fall back to the local model after a 30-second gateway timeout instead of waiting three minutes.

Independent Hermes paper research now starts successfully on Windows. Startup recovery, request preservation and long SDK paths were repaired; agent output remains research evidence and does not place orders or promote models. Separate research workspaces keep their own AI configuration.
The retired Jev rule can no longer create new virtual, Paper3 or Paper5 entries. Its historical trades remain available for review.

releases.heading: Scanner Record shows checked trade history and exposes missing evidence
items: Record separates each matching rule instead of selecting the most profitable past rule. Tap to see quote-checked closed trades, wins, losses, average win/loss, estimated costs, dates and excluded records.

Open marks, missing or invalid midpoints, duplicate records and late quotes are excluded from the historical percentage. Small samples and poor quote coverage are marked limited; virtual midpoint history is not a broker fill or a current trade probability.
Experimental local model scores are labeled separately. Old study rows show their data time instead of a new midnight match time, and stale rows no longer flash as new.
New end-of-day virtual exits retain the Strategy-exit and quote timestamps needed to audit results. Unverifiable historical trades remain excluded rather than being rewritten.

Strategy exits now request batched quotes promptly for the main, 0.20-delta and same-day contracts instead of waiting behind routine chain updates. Missing quotes retry and keep their actual timestamps. Win probability remains explicitly unvalidated until a cost-aware model passes calibration checks.

releases.heading: BOT records advance AI estimates, remembers recurring losses and retries missing quotes
items: Qualified scanner signals retry incomplete option chains within the original 10-minute deadline. Scanner-to-BOT capture shows entered, waiting and unentered signals with reasons, including daily rule caps.

New virtual trades save the local model estimate and scanner features before entry. The AI at entry column identifies the main-option Strategy-exit target; older trades without advance predictions remain Not recorded.

Learning memory keeps winning counterexamples and recurring losses separate for virtual trades, Paper 3 and Paper 5. Scanner, reviewer, critic and planner agents share saved findings; execution, RVOL, squeeze and Skittles specialists can be created when evidence calls for them.

Optional independent Hermes research is visible beside OpenClaw discussions. Agent agreement never deploys a strategy; chronological tests and future paper-fill validation remain required. No live-money trading is enabled.

releases.heading: AI research now tests actual paper fills and captures predictions at order time
items: Candidate research uses Paper 3 broker fills, filled quantities and confirmed expirations. Unfilled orders are counted separately; missing entry spreads cannot be invented or used to qualify a spread rule.

Supported entry rules compete on two earlier training periods. Only the selected candidate is checked against later dates, with costs and missed winners counted; a failed validation cannot be replaced with a runner-up chosen after seeing the results.

Paper 3 records fresh order-time inputs and experimental predictions without delaying or vetoing entries. Fast trades that close before the review poll retain their original prediction for future evaluation.

The BOT shows actual-fill data coverage and candidate training comparisons. Historical improvement alone does not activate an experiment; positive future paper results and existing promotion checks remain required.

releases.heading: BOT accounts for confirmed expiration losses and strengthens AI experiment checks
items: Paper trades reconcile broker-confirmed worthless expirations, including the missing $300 BTBT loss. Expirations are labelled separately from midpoint sell fills; missing prices remain incomplete instead of hiding losses. Carried orders always show their original date, including in Today view.

Experiments retain their original evaluation trades across restarts, require complete closed-fill evidence, and measure drawdown on closing dates. Paper 5 returns to baseline rules whenever experiment monitoring is stale or unavailable.
The BOT shows monitoring health and the next research eligibility time. Local Ollama reviews use shorter structured responses; AI research never holds up rule-qualified baseline paper entries.

releases.heading: BOT agents now run bounded experiments and evaluate future paper fills
items: Completed reviewer/critic discussions feed an experiment planner. It chooses a supported entry-spread, premium or opening-time experiment; older historical data selects the parameter and a later historical segment screens it. Historical results are exploratory, not proof of improvement.

Candidates freeze before future Paper 3 orders. A fixed ten-day evaluation counts actual paper fills, estimated fees, stressed costs, avoided losses and missed winners. Qualified candidates can automatically update Paper 5; Paper 3 remains the baseline and entries never wait for an AI response.

The BOT shows experiment status, evidence and promotion requirements. Failed candidates are rejected. Promoted candidates return to baseline if monitoring deteriorates or candidate closed losses reach $500 in a day. Existing exits and paper-only restrictions remain in force.

releases.heading: BOT columns distinguish filled trades, open losses and AI review progress
items: Paper 3 and Paper 5 ROI uses actual filled contracts, including partial entry fills. Realized P/L includes partial exits; open midpoint P/L is shown separately and stale quotes remain unpriced.

Order and fill times are separate and displayed in Eastern time. Historical observation times are labelled rather than presented as broker timestamps. Filled, ordered and held quantities are explicit.
Every trade shows its batch review state: awaiting close, not queued, queued, reviewing, reviewed or failed. An unavailable review service is never shown as a successful review.

releases.heading: BOT trades first; AI agents review completed trades afterward
items: All trades, News trade, Paper 3 and Paper 5 no longer wait for ChatGPT/Ollama approval or a 0.55 model score. Existing signal rules, risk limits, entry windows and midpoint pricing remain in force. AI pick is a comparison filter, not an entry gate.

A review agent and a critic discuss completed midpoint outcomes and actual paper fills in the background. The BOT page shows queued, reviewed and failed counts plus their latest discussion. Reviews resume after restarts; AI downtime does not block trades.
Nightly models continue learning recorded outcomes. Agent suggestions are research proposals, not automatic strategy or model changes; promotion still requires evaluation on unseen days.

releases.heading: All BOT books review new entries with OpenClaw
items: All trades, News trade, AI pick, Paper 3 and Paper 5 require OpenClaw review of new entries, using ChatGPT with local Ollama fallback after local model screening. Paper 5 is repurposed without a Jev entry filter. Missing, invalid or expired AI decisions skip entries; exits and midpoint pricing remain deterministic. Existing history stays intact, with AI reasons shown separately from legacy results.

Best price now says gains / break-even and explains why this hindsight view cannot show pre-fee losses. Use Strategy exit or Hold to close for losing outcomes. Training excludes closed trades with missing strategy-exit prices.

releases.heading: BOT separates closed results from open gains and losses
items: Strategy exit and Hold to close count wins and losses only after the selected exit is recorded. Total midpoint P/L now shows closed and open amounts separately, with an Open P/L filter for positions still held.

Exit time, reason and status follow the selected comparison. Best price is labelled hindsight and includes the recorded entry midpoint when determining the highest observed price. Missing strategy-exit quotes remain unpriced. Fractional-dollar P/L and small percentage losses remain visible instead of rounding to zero.

releases.heading: Mobile sign-in uses the credentials your password manager fills
items: Sign-in now submits the current visible email and password fields, including autofill that does not send normal typing events. An older or empty field value no longer replaces your saved credentials during submission.
Email fields identify themselves correctly to password managers and disable mobile autocapitalization and autocorrection. Existing passwords, device approval and account permissions are unchanged.

releases.heading: Clearer BOT exit choices
items: Your exit is now Strategy exit and remains selected when the BOT opens. Each exit choice has a short visible explanation, with separate spaced buttons that stack on smaller screens.

releases.heading: BOT midpoint orders, visible losses and clearer trade views
items: BOT entries and exits use midpoint limit orders, including retries. Missing quotes wait instead of falling back to market; unconfirmed cancellations keep their order tracked. Unfilled positions carry into the next session.

Zero-bid option quotes now retain their low midpoint value instead of an old trade price. The 0.20-delta view includes these losses and distinguishes missing exits from stale marks. Missing side-contract close quotes keep retrying.
Jev BOT and its comparison tab have been removed. Paper 5 takes no new entries; its existing positions and history remain available.

BOT trade loading no longer waits for historical news enrichment. Controls, win/loss totals, loading errors and mobile layout are clearer. Virtual midpoint estimates remain distinct from confirmed paper fills.

releases.heading: Recent chart candles catch up without waiting for more ticks
items: When a live price exposes missing recent candles, scanner and default-ticker charts briefly recheck the recorded history instead of waiting another ten seconds for a quote-triggered retry.
A healthy first chart request that takes more than 1.5 seconds no longer queues an unnecessary broker refresh. Empty-chart recovery still retries the stored candles.
Recent-candle recovery reads only the recent recorded window instead of copying the full retained minute archive for every chart request. Older history remains available when requested.

Recovery stops when history catches up and slows down when the source stays unchanged. Ticker changes cancel the old chart's follow-up checks; genuine no-trade intervals are never filled with invented candles.

releases.heading: Scanner charts bridge recent candle gaps sooner
items: Charts opened from the scanner can use already recorded broker minute candles immediately while deeper history and studies load. Only actual recorded candles fill gaps; no-trade intervals remain empty.

Live prices no longer advance the downloaded-history marker or suppress repeated gap recovery. Missing recent candles are requested from the last delivered history point, and ticker changes keep their own recovery state.
Background candle warm-ups now wait when the refresh queue is busy, instead of adding dozens of jobs ahead of charts you request. Default MAG7 and scanner-opened charts use the same recovery path.

Default MAG7 and quick tickers now open recent candles first. Older intraday history loads when you pan left; daily, weekly and monthly views still request their long archive. Leaving the last chart for a ticker cancels its unused chart and history-status downloads so the next ticker can connect promptly.
A queued missing-candle repair no longer turns into a full archive download.

Changing chart tickers reads stored news while the selected ticker requests a background headline refresh, instead of starting slow news scrapes that block later charts. Previous-ticker grades and summaries release their requests when you switch.
The left drawing toolbar starts hidden on desktop and phones, including after ticker changes. Use Draw to open it when needed.

releases.heading: Scanner selection stays put during saved-layout sync
items: Choosing MomX or another main navigation page now takes priority over a late startup layout reply. Saved layouts no longer send you back to Charts and restart loading after that selection.
Your saved default layout is retained and still opens when you choose Charts. Initial layout restoration keeps its existing behavior until you choose another page.

releases.heading: Scanner recovers interrupted mobile refreshes
items: Scanner reads now have their own 45-second deadline instead of being canceled at every 15-second polling interval. A slow or unexpectedly interrupted read retries once with a fresh connection and a clear message.
The last successfully loaded rows remain visible while retrying. Safari’s raw Fetch is aborted text is no longer shown for these interruptions.
Switching lists, BULL/BEAR or leaving the scanner cancels obsolete reads without displaying an error. Responses from a previous selection cannot replace the current board.
Board downloads and their JSON bodies now share the same navigation cancellation scope as the other scanner reads, releasing chart connections when you leave.
An empty or incomplete lists reply no longer clears your selected Watchlist and hides its existing rows. The last known list stays selected while metadata refreshes.

A healthy refresh with zero scan matches now keeps the full Watchlist data and real update time. Turning Scan matches only off still shows those tickers, including after a reload, instead of showing an empty board or obsolete matches.

releases.heading: Compact gamma clouds keep candles visible
items: White and orange gamma clouds no longer extend left across the chart. They stay short and thin near the right-side strike levels on desktop and mobile.
Gamma values, strike levels, text visibility and the saved glow setting keep their existing behavior.

releases.heading: Scanner Setup grades and High/Low ordering corrected
items: Scanner A+ now recognizes both green and dark-green H/L above the midpoint, and both red shades below it on BEAR. Stronger range readings no longer incorrectly lose A+. New grade results carry a rule version; saved historical records are preserved.

H/L sorting retains the full HighLowGraph value instead of rounding before ordering. Stocks near +1.00 no longer tie alphabetically simply because their displayed numbers round alike. Exact numeric ties still use symbol order.
Live H/L remembers highs and lows seen during the same two-hour bar, including when price retreats or a filter hides the row. A new two-hour window resets that live range.

Missing, disconnected, out-of-order or stale quotes no longer keep controlling H/L and its ordering. The scanner falls back to its actual board value when the live last-price update is older than 90 seconds.
Switching to BEAR now ignores hidden bullish bolt filters and the bullish H/L lightning sort, so those controls cannot silently hide or misorder bearish setups.
AI filter explanations now identify an earlier paper-trade model score and no longer present hardcoded accuracy figures or a calibrated chance of profit.

Older five-minute study inputs now show a small Data time label on the Setup cell, including the date for older sessions. A newer quote no longer hides that the displayed momentum studies came from an older candle; this label does not assert the cause is provider delay.
AI and JEV Setup filters now use the same observation time and accepted-trade checks as their Record marks.

Live quote updates now follow the top scanner rows you actually see after H/L sorting and filtering, including rows outside the backend’s original top 50 by percentage change. The 60-symbol quote limit is preserved.
Leaving the scanner or timing out a read now closes the worker response cleanly instead of attempting another reply on the canceled connection.

releases.heading: Clear scanner candle times and fewer avoidable refresh waits
items: Scanner freshness now identifies the five-minute candle window: a 07:25 timestamp covers 07:25–07:30 ET. It is no longer presented as proof of five minutes of feed delay. Older window and row times remain visible.

Live views and saved scanner boards now retain source freshness and scan completion through the display/cache path. Tooltip times include the actual browser receipt time rather than losing it during conversion.
Shared scans retain the actual source candle timestamp instead of substituting the time when volume arrived. Missing source times stay unknown.
The central TOS refresher returns an idle tape’s unused request share to tapes still waiting. The 90-request-per-minute cap is unchanged, and small lists cannot cancel larger lists’ refresh demand.
The freshness line wraps on narrow screens so its older-row information stays readable.

releases.heading: Scanner reads release chart connections when you leave
items: Leaving the scanner now cancels its outstanding records, lists, grades, momentum and other read requests, including downloads already reading their bodies. Chart candles no longer wait behind those unused scanner reads.
Read deadlines remain independent, and user-initiated saves keep their existing completion behavior.

releases.heading: AI challenger held after checking option trading costs
items: The new boosted AI candidate remains a research model after recorded bid/ask prices failed its profit check. It is withdrawn from active paper scoring, and automatic boosted promotion is disabled. The earlier local model remains experimental; neither model is presented as a reliable profit predictor. Local neural news remains enabled and paid JEV requests stay disabled.

releases.heading: Faster scanner charts without the history-loading pause
items: Charts opened from scanner tickers keep the recent candle window ready instead of automatically replaying the large research history just after opening. Pan or zoom toward earlier candles to load that history. Normal desktop chart launches and higher-timeframe history seeds retain their behavior.
Opening a compact chart from a previously cached research tape now uses the same bounded first window without discarding the stored full tape or changing prices.
Scanner freshness details now disclose that overnight TOS gaps may use BOATS history requested with a 16-minute delay, while newer available Schwab or streaming bars take precedence.
Canceled keep-alive requests close cleanly even when the browser disconnects before sending another request.

releases.heading: Cleanly cancel downloads when leaving a page
items: Canceled scanner and other page downloads now close cleanly at the API instead of being logged as an internal error and retried against a disconnected browser. Chart navigation and response contents are unchanged.

releases.heading: Verified local AI scoring and collapsed Gamma controls
items: Paper-trade AI scoring now uses a local boosted model that improved on the prior model in completed-day comparisons. It runs without paid JEV requests. Scores remain estimates, not guaranteed winning trades; an unavailable model falls back to the working local baseline.
AI Record marks retain the model and scoring time for the actual paper trade, including after a model change. Historical views reject scores calculated after the viewed time.

Gamma settings start collapsed on desktop and phones and collapse again when changing ticker or timeframe. The arrow still opens the controls; cloud visibility and the separate number-box switch are preserved.
Neural news tooltips retain the model revision and actual AI read time after relevance checks.

releases.heading: Local neural news readings and clearer gamma clouds
items: News can now be read by a local financial neural language model. AI labels show positive, negative or neutral text sentiment, with model identity and read time. Mixed, unrelated or uncertain stories do not receive a confident ticker-specific direction. Paid JEV requests remain disabled.
